The Take Snapshot button moved out of the window’s title area and into the Script History window itself — a row of its own above the snapshot list.

While a comparison is open in the editor, the Script History panel shows only the comparison summary. The snapshot list, its Compare… bar and the Take Snapshot button step aside, and all of them return the moment the compare closes.

Clicking the compare view’s own controls (Side-by-side, Unified, its close ×) no longer dismisses the Script History panel — the panel now stays put like the Scrapbook’s does, since its compare surface lives in the editor area.

While comparing, the Summary — added / deleted / modified and the scenes changed — now appears in the Script History side panel, beside the compare in the editor. The diff view no longer carries its own summary column.
Comparing starts from a single Compare… button. Click it and the list switches to picking mode; choosing your second snapshot opens the comparison right away. Rows carry no checkboxes until then.
Clicking a snapshot now shows a readable summary of what changed since the one before it — counts and scene names — instead of a wall of raw code.
The internal code on each snapshot (“86d5e36” and the like) is gone from the window. It was the snapshot’s internal id; everything now refers to snapshots by the name you gave them.

The Snapshots window is now a standard side-panel tool — same chrome, docking, and behaviour as every other tool window, instead of its own fixed sidebar. Take Snapshot sits in the tool’s header, and File ▸ Script History ▸ Snapshots opens the tool.

Comparing two snapshots now opens in the main editor area, inside the app chrome — its Side-by-side / Unified / Changes controls can no longer collide with the ribbon or the window title bar. The Snapshots tool stays open beside it, and closing the compare returns the editor.

Snapshots can be deleted. Every row in the Snapshots window has a Delete button, and the list has Delete All… — the one-click way to clear out the old “Auto save” entries earlier versions wrote into the list. Both warn first, and neither ever touches your script — a snapshot is a copy.
A snapshot taken from the Snapshots window’s own button now appears in the list immediately — no closing and reopening.
Note: auto saves stopped being written into this list in v6.72; entries from before that stay until you delete them.

Auto saves are no longer snapshots. The auto-save timer used to take a version check-in — the very same thing File ▸ Take Snapshot does — so every auto save turned up in the Snapshots window. It now writes only timestamped files to the Auto Save Locations you choose, and never touches your snapshots.
The “Local version history (always on)” auto-save location is gone; that row was what put auto saves into the Snapshots window.
The Snapshots window has its own “+ Take Snapshot” button in the top left.

Save Options: the auto-save folder row is called “Local device folder” and offers one Choose Folder… button instead of two, the Auto Save Locations helper text is gone, and the auto-save description says what an auto save actually is.

“Maximum Project Versions” has been removed — it counted the version check-ins auto saving no longer makes. Capping the auto-save FILES is still to come; it needs a folder-listing permission the desktop shell does not grant yet.
The Annotations window’s “Display” button is now called “Filter” — the same word the ribbon’s Annotation Filter uses for the same choice, so one idea has one name.

Settings ▸ Presets gained four more things to tick: Annotation Presets (the icon and colour combinations offered when you add an annotation), Keyboard Shortcuts, Design (the sizes and spacing from the Design window) and Helper Text (tooltips you have rewritten or hidden). Nine items now, all in the one preset file.
An item you have not touched yet is shown but can’t be ticked, and says why — so an empty category can never be silently “exported”.

Snapshots no longer hangs on “Loading snapshots…”. Script History talks to a ScriptCraft server, and the desktop app doesn’t run one — the window now says so straight away instead of waiting on a request that can never arrive.
Any snapshot load is time-limited, so whatever the connection does the window ends up saying something you can act on, with a Try Again button rather than a dead end.
The ribbon’s “Annotation Visibility” button is now called “Annotation Filter” — which is what it does: pick which annotation types and statuses show on the script.

New “View Annotations” button: a plain on/off toggle for annotations on the script, lit when they show, with an eye that closes when they don’t. It is the same setting as View ▸ Annotations ▸ Show Annotations in Script, so the two always agree.
If your ribbon already had the filter button, the new toggle takes its place right beside it — no trip to Customize needed.

Annotation icons now follow the page zoom. They stayed exactly where they were when you zoomed, so at 90% an icon could end up sitting inside a line of dialogue — they now stay on the row they annotate, in the page’s left margin, at every zoom.
The icons also scale with the page, keeping the same size relative to the text instead of swelling as you zoom out.
They re-place themselves after any layout change too — opening a panel, resizing the window, changing the page setup.

Send to Script now anchors each section annotation at the TOP OF THE PAGE that section starts on. With three one-page sections you get one at the top of page 1, one at the top of page 2 and one at the top of page 3. It had been landing on whichever scene happened to cover that page, which is not the same thing.
An element left carrying a deleted annotation’s anchor no longer blocks that spot for good — a section can anchor there again.

Send to Script now makes real ANNOTATIONS — one per outline section, anchored at the page the outline puts that section on, reading “Act I — 40 pages”. v6.64 wrote “# …” section lines into the script instead; that was the wrong thing, and nothing is written into your script text any more.

Each annotation keeps mirroring its section: rename it or change its page estimate and the annotation updates on the spot, whether the Outline Bar is open or not. Annotations you made yourself are never touched.

The next Send to Script clears out any “# …” lines v6.64 left behind, so nothing is listed twice. Sending again updates what is there and adds only what is missing; deleting a section leaves its annotation alone.

Send to Script now puts your outline SECTIONS into the script — one section line each, at the page the outline puts that section on, carrying its name and its estimated pages (“# Act I — 40 pages”). It used to append one line per beat at the end of the script.

Those lines stay live. Rename a section, or change its page estimate, and the line in the script rewrites itself on the spot — no need to send again, and it works whether the Outline Bar is open or not.

Pressing Send to Script again updates the lines already there and adds only what is missing, so you can never end up with duplicates. Deleting a section in the outline leaves its line in your script exactly as written — the mirror never deletes your text.

Settings ▸ Presets is now a checklist that makes ONE preset file. Tick the items you want included — Settings, Customizations, Themes, Workspaces, Outline Presets — and Export Preset writes them all into a single file. Six separate exports and six separate files are gone.
An item you have none of yet is shown but can’t be ticked, and says why. Export stays dead until something is ticked, so you can never write an empty preset.

Import Preset takes one file and applies whatever is in it, after telling you what that is. It still opens every preset file ScriptCraft has ever written — old full presets, settings backups, customization, theme, workspace and outline-preset files all load as the item they hold.

Outline: deleting a section no longer makes it look like its beats jumped into the section next door. They were always going to Unsorted — but the surviving section stretched across the board and wrapped its cards into a grid, which read exactly like everything had been dumped there. A section only takes the whole board when it really is the only column, Unsorted included.
Outline: every column on the board now starts at the same width, Unsorted included. Its width used to be set by its own contents, so the one-line hint stretched it wider than the sections beside it.

Outline: columns resize by dragging their right edge, and the edge is now a proper 10px target that lights up when you are on it — the old handle sat half outside the column, which clipped it down to a 3px sliver you had to hit exactly. Unsorted resizes too. A section’s width saves with the script.

Deleting an outline section no longer deletes the beats inside it. They move to “Unsorted” — the dashed column furthest left on the board — in the order they were in, and you drag them wherever they belong. It is a single undo step, and the trash button now says so before you click it.
The one and only way to delete a beat is the delete button on the beat itself.
The holding column for beats with no section is now called Unsorted (it was Uncategorized).

Outline presets now use the beats you already have. Choosing a structure over an existing outline re-homes your cards into its sections and re-fits their page estimates to fit — instead of dumping them in “Uncategorized” and laying a second set of blank cards on top. Every section comes out filled, its beats still add up to its page budget exactly, and nothing is created or deleted. It is still one undo step.

Beats are spread across the new sections in proportion to their page budgets, in the order they were already in — with more beats than sections, the bigger sections get more of them; with fewer, the sections carrying the most story get one each.

Page estimates now belong to each outline variation. Changing how many pages a beat spans on one variation no longer changes it on the others — the same beat can be a two-pager in one arrangement and a six-pager in another. Editing on the Outline Bar writes the variation the bar is showing, not the one open on the board.

Outline: closing a variation tab is called what it is — deleting. The confirm reads "Delete Outline Tab" with a Delete Tab button, and the × on a tab says "Delete this outline variation (beats are kept)". Nothing about the behaviour changed: your beats live in every tab, and only that arrangement of sections goes.

Outline presets now arrive filled in: the 3-Act Structure lays down 20 beats in each act at 2 pages apiece, and every other preset is filled the same way — about two pages a beat — so a section's beats always add up to exactly the pages that section is budgeted. (Save the Cat's one-page beats get a single card; its 25-page Fun and Games gets thirteen.) Presets you save yourself fill the same way.
Applying a preset is a single undo step, however many cards it lays down.
Outline: a divider line separates the outline tabs from the + button.

Outline: the beat count ("4 beats") is plain text again — it had been sitting inside the tab strip's outline, which drew a box around it. It now sits clear of the + button and is vertically centered in the header.

Outline ▸ Freeform: beat titles are smaller in the card's title bar, and the title no longer stretches across the whole bar — there's always a clear strip of bare bar to grab when you want to move the card. Click the title and it expands to the full width for editing; a long title shows with an ellipsis at rest.

Outline ▸ Freeform: every beat card now has a proper title bar across the top — its own shaded band holding the title and the card's buttons — and the whole bar is the handle you grab to move the card around the board.

The bar sits above a beat's picture, the way a window's title bar does, and it tints itself to match colored cards in every theme. The old ⋮⋮ grip is gone from freeform cards, since the bar replaces it (cards in the Sections view keep theirs).

Outline ▸ Freeform: dragging a card by its header works now — anywhere along the top row, like every window in the app. (The v6.52 attempt let the browser's own text-selection take over the gesture whenever you started on the title; nothing native starts there any more. Clicking the title still puts the cursor exactly where you clicked.)
Outline ▸ Freeform: cards resize from any edge or corner, not just the bottom-right — and dragging the top or left edge moves that side while the opposite one stays put.

Outline ▸ Freeform: the Connect button moved to the card's bottom-right corner, and connecting is now click-place-click — click Connect, click where you want the line to leave the first card, then click where it should meet the second. A circle follows your pointer along each card's edge so you can see the exact spot; Escape cancels.

Connections remember those points in proportion to the card, so resizing a card keeps its lines attached where you put them. Connections made before this update keep drawing from card center to card center.
Outline: the beat count sits at the left of the header now, right of the tabs.

Beat cards stand off the board background clearly in every theme — the card surface takes a fixed step toward the theme's text color, plus a soft shadow, so the separation holds whichever theme you use. Cards you've colored yourself are unchanged.

Helper Text is a real tool window now: drag it into a side panel like any other, pop it back out, fullscreen it, and its size is remembered. It still opens from Help ▸ Developer ▸ Helper Text… — and it no longer closes when you open another window (it stays up while its go-to buttons open the window a piece of text lives in).
Outline ▸ Freeform: while you're drawing a connection, the card you started from stays highlighted and the card under your pointer lights up — so it's clear which card you're about to connect to.
Outline ▸ Freeform: cards drag from anywhere along their top row, like every window in the app, instead of only the little corner grip. Clicking the title still puts the cursor in it for editing.

Helper Text: the window now lists every fixed tooltip and placeholder in the app — including the ~100 that were written as dynamic expressions (like the outline bar checkbox's hover text) and never showed up before. Editing them takes effect live, as always.
Helper Text: fixed a bug where a control whose tooltip changes with its state (checked vs unchecked) could show the wrong custom text after the state flipped.
Helper Text: the Outline window's ? help text is editable now too.
Standing rule going forward: any change that adds or removes helper text updates the Helper Text window's catalog as part of the same change — a build check enforces it.

Outline: the view control in the header now shows just the current view's icon and name — Sections or Freeform — like every other window; the word "View" is gone, and both options carry icons in the menu.
Outline: + Add Section leads the body row at the far left, with breathing room before the Presets dropdown.
Outline: the checkbox now reads "Show this outline in the outline bar".
Outline: the header now carries the standard control set — a View dropdown (Sections / Freeform, replacing the Arrangement label and buttons), a Filter dropdown, and Search.

Outline: Filter narrows the board by beat color (it lists the colors your outline actually uses, with swatches), and Search matches beat titles and descriptions — in Sections, Uncategorized, and Freeform alike. The beat count reads "3 of 12 beats" while either is active.
Outline: the Presets dropdown and + Add Section moved down into the first row of the window body, and "Show in Outline Bar" sits at that row's right edge.
Outline: the "Show beat color on all tabs" checkbox is gone — a beat's color always fills its whole card.
View menu: "Theme" is now "Themes".
Customize ▸ Themes: clicking a theme switches the app to it (the row's Edit/Delete/Hide buttons keep their own jobs). Clicking a hidden theme applies it and moves it back to Shown.

Outline: the variation tabs moved up into the window header, like every other window's tabs — with the + button beside them; double-click a tab to rename it, × closes it. In a narrow window they collapse into the standard dropdown pill.

Outline: the little ◉ on each tab is gone — a "Show in Outline Bar" checkbox in the header now says whether the tab you're viewing feeds the Outline Bar. One tab always does, so the box locks while it's the one shown; check it on another tab to switch.
Outline: applying a preset names the tab after it (pick 3-Act Structure and the tab says 3-Act Structure).
Outline: the Presets dropdown wears the same background as every other dropdown (it was transparent).

Script History: every "Auto Save" here is now a "Snapshot" — Take Snapshot…, Snapshots, Compare with Snapshot…, Track Changes Since Last Snapshot, plus the dialog and window text. (The timed auto-save feature and its Auto Saves folder on disk keep their names.)

Fixed: the Outline window header's controls could collapse to nothing in a floating window (a long-standing layout bug the new header tabs exposed), and header tabs across all windows collapsed into the dropdown earlier than the window's width required.

Three new built-in themes, from the palette analysis: Paper (a true paper-white light theme — near-white surfaces, ink-dark text, a deep blue accent), Gruvbox Dark (the warm retro dark palette — cream text and an amber accent on brown-charcoal), and Catppuccin Mocha (the soft blue-purple dark palette with a mauve accent). All three pass the same 4.5:1 text-contrast floor and surface-ladder checks as the existing themes. Pick them in View ▸ Theme, or manage them in Customize ▸ Themes.

Theme legibility pass (from the palette analysis; only the theme suggestions were applied): Sepia's muted text and accent deepen to meet the 4.5:1 accessibility floor (3.37→5.01 and 3.68→5.89); Solarized Light gets deeper steps of its own hues for text (4.99→6.15) and muted text (2.48→4.64); Dracula's muted text and Light's muted text each move one step (4.46→5.30, 4.43→5.08 on panels). Hues and the character of every theme are unchanged — these are depth adjustments, not new colors. The note-chip, annotation and scene-swatch suggestions were NOT applied.

Characters: the Upload Voice Clip tool is removed from the character window. The Voice Profile section keeps its Speech Pattern and Vocabulary fields; already-uploaded clips stay in your saved files and the Asset Manager, they just no longer have a player here.

File ▸ Print: another crash cause removed — the print job was being created with an empty print configuration, the one step all three crashing builds shared (before the dialog ever differed between them). It now uses the system's shared print settings, the way every working macOS print path does.

If printing ever fails again, the app now writes a step-by-step trace to a small file as it goes — the last line of that file names the exact step that died, so the next fix comes from evidence, not deduction.
Settings… sits second-to-last in the ScriptCraft menu, directly above Quit (it briefly moved to the File menu in v6.43 — that's reversed).

File ▸ Print: found and fixed the remaining crash. The print sheet is presented asynchronously, and the app was releasing the print operation the instant it had scheduled the sheet — macOS then tried to show a dialog for an object that no longer existed. The operation now stays alive for the sheet's whole life. (This was a memory-lifetime bug, invisible to the previous fix's error handling.)
Settings… now lives in the File menu as the second-to-last item (Script History is last), with the standard ⌘, shortcut. It leaves the ScriptCraft app menu.
The Settings and Helper Text windows wear the exact same full-screen and close buttons as every other window — the standard icon set, not lookalikes.

Settings is a real window now — drag its header to move it, pull any edge to resize, and use the standard full-screen and close buttons. Same chrome as every other window (one shared shell, also behind the Helper Text window).

Save Options: the folder for 'Local System (always on)' is changeable — the row shows the chosen folder with a Choose Folder… button. It edits the same folder Save As uses, so the two never disagree. (The checkbox stays on: the app's own library copy always saves.)

The account and cloud-server surfaces are gone everywhere: the ScriptCraft Account section in Save Options, the 'Cloud' save and autosave options, the System tab's server URL / sign-in / devices sections, the sign-in chip in the status bar, and the Open window's cloud tab. ScriptCraft is fully local (Google Drive and OneDrive copies remain, connected directly to those providers).
Auto saves to a local folder now land in an 'Auto Saves' folder inside your chosen location instead of loose beside your files. The folder is created automatically.
Annotations window: the Filter button is named Display.

Save Options are always editable: fixed — a cloud location picked during document setup (OneDrive, Google Drive, Cloud) could show checked but LOCKED in Settings, impossible to uncheck until you connected. No checkbox in Save Options disables itself any more; the row hints still say what a location needs before it can actually receive saves.

New save location: 'Local System (backup location)' — a second folder on this device that receives a copy of the script on every save. Checking it opens the folder picker; the chosen path shows beside the row, and the Save window's location chips include it.
The 'Show/Hide Annotations' button is removed from the ribbon toolbar options (annotation visibility still lives in the Annotation Visibility menu and the Annotations window).

Collaboration is REMOVED. The unreleased real-time collaboration feature — the File ▸ Collaboration menu, invite links, the live-session banner, the Collaboration Server and Invite Defaults settings sections, and the sync machinery behind them — is gone from the app entirely. Your ScriptCraft account, Cloud saves, and sign-in are unaffected (they never depended on collaboration; the settings sections are now titled 'ScriptCraft Account').

Locations ▸ Map: the import-time rotation bar ('Turn the map upright…', Rotate, Set Rotation) is gone — rotation lives in the header's Options menu and can be changed at ANY time. The pins turn with the map, so nothing drifts off its landmark, and a fresh import is ready for pinning immediately.

Locations ▸ Map: fixed — rotating the map could still make it disappear in the app (it drew fine in ordinary browsers, so this was the desktop engine mishandling the CSS rotation). The map is now DRAWN onto a canvas — the rotation happens in the drawing itself, with no CSS transform left for the engine to get wrong.
Helper Text window: the standard window header — title, full-screen button, close button — like every other tool window.

Helper text can now be BLANK: clear a field and that item simply has no helper text. The reset button (↺) still restores the app's own wording. (The stray 'video' row is gone from the list — it was an internal accessibility label on embedded videos in Script Notes, not real helper text.)

Snippets: two buttons at the top — Cut selection to snippet and Copy selection — doing what ⌥⌘X/⌥⌘C already did, plus an insert button on every snippet card that places its text at the cursor exactly like dragging it in.
Outline: + Add Section (and + Add Beat) wear the standard blue button.

Locations ▸ Map: fixed — rotating the map could shrink it to a speck in a short window ('made it disappear'); the map now keeps a visible minimum size and scrolls instead. Rotation also recovers automatically from a transient image-load failure, and map images no longer reload on every redraw.

Locations ▸ Map: Map Options moved into the window header as 'Options'; the Grouped/Ungrouped toggle sits at the right edge of the pin row; and each sidebar item's Map / Pin / Group buttons are replaced by one ⋮ menu in the item header holding all their options.
Side panel: dragging the adjustment bar vertically now resizes the CONTENTS of the open tool window along with the row titles.

Fixed: File ▸ Print crashed the app. The print dialog was being run as an app-blocking loop from inside the window system's own event handling, and errors from macOS's print machinery could kill the process outright. The dialog now presents as a sheet on the main window, the work runs off the main thread, and any macOS-side error falls back to opening the PDF instead of crashing.

File ▸ Print now opens the system print dialog directly — no PDF viewer in between. The desktop shell prints the exact export through macOS's own PDF engine, so what the dialog shows is the same page the exporter builds: true margins, page numbers, Courier Prime. If the dialog ever can't come up (say, the shell hasn't rebuilt yet), it falls back to opening the PDF, then to the save dialog — never a silent nothing.
Annotations: the on-page icon moved from the right margin to the left — centered in the left margin band, clear of the page edge, the text, and the scene-number zone.

Fixed: updating could abort with "Your local changes would be overwritten by merge" — the desktop launcher runs npm install on every start, and npm rewrites frontend/package-lock.json slightly differently per machine, leaving it permanently modified. The launcher now restores that file before pulling, the same way it already restores Cargo.lock. (The committed copies are canonical; nothing on the Mac is meant to edit either.)

Text now wraps exactly like the reference program. Measured from the comparison page: true 10-characters-per-inch Courier with full-width lines running 1.5" to 7.8" — 63 characters, where ScriptCraft was fitting 60–61. The letter-spacing squeeze is gone, the right margin default is 0.7", and the editor, the page count, and PDF/Word exports now share ONE geometry source, so the same paragraph breaks on the same words everywhere. The sample line — "…cafeteria. He hears a" — ends its rows exactly as the reference does.
Fixed: the PDF exporter wrapped one word early on full lines — it counted each word's trailing space when deciding fit. That, plus the narrower column, is why "of" landed on a third row.

Fixed: Asset Manager images were still broken. Real cause found in the desktop shell's file-serving code: it stripped every leading slash from the decoded path, turning it relative — reads worked only by luck of the working directory. Paths are re-anchored (and locked to the app's own data folder). If a stored file is ever genuinely missing, the list now says so instead of showing an eternal broken-image glyph — and thumbnails self-heal by re-reading bytes through the proven storage road if the file protocol ever misbehaves again.

File ▸ Print on the desktop now writes the print-ready PDF and OPENS it in your PDF viewer — Preview comes up on the exact export, one ⌘P from the real print dialog. (The desktop shell gains a small opener plugin; first launch after updating recompiles it.) If opening fails, the save dialog fallback remains.

Editor text renders at print weight on macOS (antialiased smoothing) and Courier Prime now leads the font stack — the same face embedded in exports, so screen and paper match. The perceived darkness vs the reference is mostly the reference using a thinner Courier cut; the squeeze removal and smoothing close most of the gap.
Title Page editor: Fit now respects both width and height — the whole page always lands inside the preview.
Scene numbers in exports anchor 0.15" off the heading column on both sides, matching the editor exactly.

Fixed: images in the Asset Manager showed a broken question mark, in the list and in the preview. The desktop app's file protocol for reading stored assets was never switched on — it is now, scoped to the app's own assets folder.

Fixed: File ▸ Print on the desktop app now saves a print-ready PDF through the normal save dialog and says so — the in-app print window can't open in the desktop shell, and the previous attempts failed silently. Exact margins and page numbers; open the file and press ⌘P.
Exports now embed Courier Prime — the same face the app shows — instead of leaving PDF viewers to substitute Courier Std. Layout and character widths are unchanged.
Asset Manager: image files show a real thumbnail in the list — click it for the full preview.

Formatting, verified against the standard: the font was already right (Courier, true 12pt on a 12pt line grid) — the visible difference against other programs was scene-heading spacing. Scene headings now carry the spec's TWO blank lines before them, in the editor, the page count, and exported PDFs alike. Scripts repaginate slightly longer; that's the standard.
FADE IN: sits at the left margin now — it's the opening transition. Every other transition (CUT TO:, FADE OUT.) stays right-aligned, and retyping a transition re-aligns it live. Exports match.

Fixed: File ▸ Print did nothing in the desktop app — the print window was being blocked silently. Printing now works there, and if the print view ever can't open, ScriptCraft saves a print-ready PDF and tells you.

Fixed: printing shrank the page. The system print dialog was fitting our full 8.5×11 page inside its own printer margins — the double-margin effect. File ▸ Print now renders the same exact-layout PDF the exporter makes and opens it with the print dialog ready, so paper matches the file (page numbers included). Exporting was never affected — the exported file has exact margins and true 12pt type.
Goals: "Show in: Header" now means the actual app header — the title-bar line with the script name and quick access toolbar — with the chip at its right edge.

Fixed: importing a PDF failed with "undefined is not a function (near '...value of readableStream...')". The PDF engine's modern build assumes browser features the desktop app's WebKit doesn't have — it runs on the compatibility build now, same import, same results.

Title Page: the editor scales with the Pages window now — the form column is sized to fit its fields (no more horizontal scroll bar), the preview takes all the remaining room and re-fits as you resize, and narrow windows stack the two columns. The Contact field's ghost text also shows its four example lines properly instead of literal \n.

Fixed: File ▸ Asset Manager did nothing. It was being seated in a side-panel slot that panels refuse to render — invisible, and the leftover slot made the next click a silent no-op too. It opens as its own window now, as does Tools ▸ Spelling & Grammar ▸ Spell Check Panel, which shared the bug.
Title Page: the Contact field is four rows tall — room for name, agency, email and phone without scrolling.

Goals: breathing room below the Start button and above the Quick start section, and the empty band under the Vomit Draft row is gone — the pane was stacking its own bottom padding on the window's, which read as a phantom row. The window's default size also grew to fit the new layout.
Helper Text: the list is organized by where things are found — Ribbon Toolbar, Menus, Status Bar, each tool window, and so on — in collapsible groups.

Helper Text: the found-in info is written on each row now (not just on hover), and every row has a hide button so items you've reviewed can be cleared from the list — the Hidden view lists them and puts them back.
Helper Text: rows that live in an openable window carry a go-there button — it opens that window without closing Helper Text.
Helper Text: line breaks are allowed — the edit field grows as you type (Enter makes a new line), and multi-line text renders its breaks in tooltips and hints.

Goals: one ▶ Start button at the top-left of the window — it becomes ■ Stop while a goal runs (Dismiss when it's done) and starts whatever the current tab is set to. The Header/Footer choice sits on the same row, right-aligned, and the footer is just the Vomit Draft checkbox now.
Goals: the Words and Pages tabs have Quick start rows — one click starts a write-this-much-more goal from wherever the script stands (250–5,000 words, 1–10 pages).
Helper Text moved into its own window — Help ▸ Developer ▸ Helper Text… — with search, kind filters and every string shown at once (no more "N more" note).
Each helper-text row now leads with the control it belongs to: the button's icon and visible text where there is one, otherwise the window it lives in — so you can tell which item you're editing.
Goals: the Reach word / Reach page rows show the script's current total, right-aligned — set an absolute target while looking at where you stand.
Goals: the window footer is one row, and the readout placement options are named Header / Footer now. In the header, the goal chip sits at the right edge of the ribbon.

The Design window gained a Helper Text section: every hover tooltip, field ghost text, empty-list hint, the script's element hints (Action…, CHARACTER NAME, …) and the ? help text — 386 strings, searchable, each editable with its own reset. Edits apply live everywhere the text appears, persist across restarts, and Reset helper text puts everything back.

Thesaurus: opening the tool with a word already highlighted looks that word up right away — no more open-first, select-after. The editor's right-click menu also gained a Thesaurus entry, customizable like every other context-menu item.
Analytics: the Overview / Scenes / Dialogue / Gender tabs moved into the window header, like every other tabbed window.

Fixed: pasting into the script with an action element active no longer drops the text below it as an unstyled block with the wrong spacing. Pasted paragraphs — from plain text or another app — now land as proper action elements, filling the active empty element in place; pasting mid-sentence joins the first paragraph into the element you're in. Dropped snippets follow the same rule.

Fixed: dragging a snippet into the script pasted its internal id — a UUID — instead of its words. The drag now carries the snippet's text, line breaks intact, and the card stays on its shelf. A note card dragged into the script arrives as its readable text too.

Fixed: when a window's header tabs had collapsed into the dropdown, widening the window never brought the tabs back — in the side panel or popped out. The header's stretchy spacer was being measured at its stretched width, so the space the tabs needed always appeared to grow with the window and the fit test could never pass.
The Working Notes submenu is gone from the View menu.
Goals: every tab has "Show in:" — Footer keeps the goal readout in the status bar as before; Toolbar parks the same chip at the right end of the ribbon.

Goals: the Words and Pages tabs are an either/or like Time — "Reach page:" / "Reach word:" (the absolute total, as before) or "Finish N Pages" / "Write N Words", which completes when the script grows by that much from wherever it stood when you pressed Start.
Goals: a 60 min quick-start joined the Time tab, the Vomit Draft checkbox lives in the window footer, and the ? button is gone.

Fixed: a stray three-dot "More format options" button appeared at the ribbon's right edge for layouts that still carried the retired highlighter — the empty slot measured as a hidden item and summoned the overflow menu. The retired token is filtered out entirely now.

The menus are reorganized. Project: Navigator, Pages, Scenes, Locations, Characters, Snippets, Set Draft Number, Title Page, Custom Page. Tools: Outline, Notes, Scrapbook, Annotations, Goals, Focus, Analytics, Spelling & Grammar, Thesaurus. Production stands on its own again: Revision Mode, Production Tags, Lock Scene Numbers, Lock Pages. Insert Image and Insert Element moved into Edit, and the Insert menu is gone. Customize… returned to the top of the View menu, and Action Rewrite lives under Help ▸ Developer.

Characters: the List view lost its box outlines — flat rows with the same faint divider lines the Scenes list draws. Cards got a quieter, dimmer outline and now sit on their own surface, a step lighter than the window background. And the View menu lists List first.

The Characters window header grew its missing controls. Profiles: a Filter (In script only · With an image · With a description). Relationships: Filter (by relationship type), Sort (Character A–Z or Type) and Search — the search matches either character's name, and the list and map both obey all three.

The Characters window's List view is the same table the Scenes and Locations lists use: a Character column you can drag-resize, an inline Description field on every row (it writes the same description the full profile edits, as plain text), and "Times used:" with the scene count. Clicking a row still expands the full profile beneath it.

The Highlights tool is gone — highlighting lives in the Annotations tool now. The tool window, its Tools-menu entry, the Format ▸ Highlighting submenu and the ribbon's script highlighter are all removed. Old-style highlights in existing scripts still render (the mark stays), and the Scrapbook keeps its text-background picker (the ribbon item is "Box Background (Scrapbook)" now, shown only while the Scrapbook is open).

Preview: "Template Options" is "Script Options" now, and the include list is "Include Annotations…" — one row per current annotation type (with its icon), checking a type shows its highlights in the preview. The old include toggles are gone: sections, markers, notes and script to-dos never appear in Preview, and scene numbers follow the editor's own scene-number setting.

The big two-row ribbon buttons all wear one exact format now: the same distance between icon and name on every button, and hovering any of them highlights the icon and name together as one block. Before, buttons built from the toolbar's built-in controls drew their name outside the button — so the hover box wrapped only the icon, and the spacing drifted from the pinned-tool buttons.

Fixed: dragging the Analytics window (or any temporary tool window) teleported it half its width leftward on the first move, leaving the grab cursor floating off the window's right edge. Temporary windows are CSS-centered; the drag now clears that centering the moment it takes over, so the window tracks the pointer exactly. The same fix covers resizing them by an edge.

Fixed: dropping the Analytics window on a side panel left the window open — the drop registered, but Analytics' old always-open-as-a-window rule immediately re-floated it. An explicit dock now wins: the window leaves, the tool lands in the panel, and it reopens there until you drag it back out.

Fixed: windows without header controls — Snippets, Thesaurus, Highlights, AI Writer, Workspaces — had their header strip crushed to a sliver, with the fullscreen and close buttons spilling over the body. Every window's header now holds the standard height; all windows were swept and measured to confirm.
Locations map: the Map Options button wears the same blue format as + Add Pin.
The Group dropdown's second section is "Other Groups" now.

Grouping is an Ungrouped / Grouped toggle on the first row of the Locations window body — in the List view and at the top of the Map view alike. Ungrouped, the map's location list shows every script location on its own row; Grouped folds connected locations back into one row per place.
The Insert menu dropped its old Section, Marker, Note and To-Do List entries — those live with their tools.

Fixed: Insert ▸ Custom Page did nothing visible on a fresh script (it inserted at the caret, which sat inside the title page region). It opens a small window now asking where the page goes — after which page — and inserts through the same machinery as the Pages tool.

Fixed: an armed annotation (the + button with nothing selected) ignored your selection if the mouse release landed outside the page edge. It hears the release anywhere now — select the text and the annotation window opens.

The Thesaurus runs on Princeton WordNet itself now, and every sense shows its definition above the synonyms — so choosing between senses no longer means guessing from the synonym list. Antonyms still sit on their own row, everything still lives on your machine.
The Goals window's Words / Pages / Time tabs sit on the left of the header now, like every other window's tabs (and collapse into the same labeled dropdown when the window is narrow).

Fixed: the Customize window opens on the tab you used last — remembered across restarts. It never worked because every menu door forced it back to a fixed tab on the way in; the plain "Customize…" doors no longer steer it, and the targeted ones (Customize Themes…, Customize Elements…) still land on their tab.
The expanded location's buttons read Map · Pin · Group on one row — Group is the old "+ Connect to location", moved up beside them. The List view's dropdown leads with the same Group button.

The map view's location list carries the same expanded details as the List view now — Location Group, script locations, Connect to location, description, and custom fields, right under the Map Options and Pin Options buttons. One block, both views; editing it in either place edits the same location.

Fixed: the fullscreen map's location list always appeared in the LEFT side panel. It hangs directly under the Locations row now, in whichever panel you keep the Locations window — and without a second "Locations" header, since the row above is the label.

Fixed: the fullscreen map's side-panel location list rendered as a second column beside the tool list, doubling the left side and squeezing the map. It sits inside the panel now, and the map takes the full width.
The scene list is out of the expanded location row.
Fullscreen on the map, the location list stands in the side panel — the way the Scrapbook's navigator does — and the map takes the full width.
"Display Name" is "Location Group" now: create a group, or add the location to one that exists. Ungroup dissolves the name; the locations stay connected.
Location custom fields ask their scope, like character fields: this location only, or all locations.
The filter's INT. and EXT. sit on one row as toggles — selecting one shows only it; neither (or both) shows everything.
The filter can narrow to a single location group, or to No Group.

Map view: expanding a sidebar location now shows two buttons in the top row of its body — Map Options and Pin Options. The editing fields that were in the sidebar moved to the Locations panel: expand any location in the list and everything the place knows is there — display name, its script locations, Connect to location, description, and custom fields.
List view: the Group button lives in the window header now, right of the View control, and lights up while grouping is on.
Grouped, every location has a home: anything that doesn't belong to a named group gathers under "No Group" at the end of the list.
Pop-up menus share one set of rules now. The Goals help pop-up gained three behaviours it never had: it closes when you press elsewhere, when you scroll, and on Escape.
Groundwork: the remaining nineteen pop-ups can now adopt the same rules one at a time.

Twenty-one dialogs now share one shell. Nine of them could not be closed with Escape at all before — Page Setup, Compare Versions, the dictionary panels, the grammar rules panel and the storage warnings among them.
Selecting text inside a dialog and releasing the mouse outside it no longer closes the dialog and discards what you were doing.

Dialogs share one shell now. The first three moved onto it — About, Changelog and Mores & Continueds — and all three gained two things they never had: Escape closes them, and selecting text inside one no longer dismisses it when you release the mouse outside.
Dropped two build-only dependencies that only a single inspection script used.
Removed 202 lines of stylesheet belonging to controls that no longer exist.
The temporary placement readout is off the map. It went on to catch a fault that could not be reproduced here; no pin has landed in the wrong place since, so it has done its job.
Each row in the map sidebar now carries two icon buttons: a map icon for the place — Connect to location, Hide from locations list — and a pin icon for where it sits — Lock/Unlock pin, Delete pin.
Hiding a location keeps it and its pin; it only leaves the lists. "Show hidden locations" in the Filter menu brings it back.
The Locations list always shows the script's own location name now. A new "Group" button folds locations that share a display name under it, with the display name as the heading.

A new pin now checks itself: after it is drawn, the app compares where the marker actually is against where you clicked, and moves it onto the click if they differ. It no longer matters which measurement of the map is wrong.
Temporary: the map shows a small readout of the last placement's numbers. It is there to identify a fault that cannot be reproduced outside Derek's machine, and comes out once it has.

A new pin can no longer be put on the map's edge by a bad measurement. Where you clicked is now worked out three independent ways, and each direction is taken from a reading that actually puts the click on the map — so one wrong reading can't decide it.
If any reading does disagree, the app now says so in the developer console instead of quietly moving the pin.

Fixed: a pin could still land at the top edge of the map instead of where you clicked, while the dropdown opened in the right place. The dropdown was placed from the click itself; the pin was placed from a separately measured position of the map, and when the two disagreed the pin was pushed to the edge. The pin now comes from the same click the dropdown does.
The ghost pin and the placed pin are worked out the same way, so where the ghost sits is where the pin lands.
Fixed: a trackpad click on a pin counted as a tiny drag — it nudged the pin and swallowed the click that should have opened its dropdown.

Fixed: a pin appeared above the map instead of where you clicked. Arming "+ Add Pin" made the button's row taller, which pushed the map down; placing the pin shrank the row again and the map jumped back up under it. The row's height no longer changes.
One press of "+ Add Pin", one pin — clicking the map otherwise is just a click.
Map Options moved out of the window header down beside "+ Add Pin": Replace Map (from your device or the Asset Manager), Rotate 90 degrees, and Delete Map with a warning first.
Rotating the map now turns the pins with it, so each one stays on its own feature.
The map sidebar's lock is a lock/unlock icon with a delete button beside it, and its redundant "LOCATIONS" title and count are gone — the window header already says both.

The Locations list is the same table as Scenes: the location, a drag-resizable Description column, and "Times used:". The description is the same one the map sidebar shows, and it now follows its location onto the map instead of being left behind.
Every tool window's header buttons are now in one order — View, Filter, Sort, Search — whichever of them that window has. Characters and Scenes had drifted.

"+ Connect to location" now lists EVERY script location — including ones already on the map, saying which pin they'd move from — plus your location groups, where picking one joins this place to that group.
The pin dropdown offers the same list, so connecting works the same way from either place.

Fixed: a pin in the right half of the map drew well left of its own point, and locking it moved it further — it could slide off the map. The marker now sits exactly on its point whichever way the label runs.
+ Add Pin is a blue button and arms placement: the pin follows the cursor and a click sets it down. Escape cancels.
Fixed: after dragging a pin, the next click on the map could be ignored.
Locations that share a pin are now ONE row in the sidebar, with a count — not one row each.
Opening that row lists its script locations, and connects another one from there.
A + Add Pin button drops a pin in the middle of the map; clicking the map still works too.
Fixed: attaching a location moved the pin. The marker now stays exactly on its point whatever the label says, and labels near the right edge turn inward.
Fixed: dragging a pin dropped a second pin where you let go.
Pins can be locked — from the pin's dropdown or the sidebar — so a stray drag can't move them. A locked pin still opens its dropdown, which is where it unlocks.
Locations: List and Map are now the header's View dropdown instead of tabs.
A newly imported map can be rotated before you commit to it — once you press Set Rotation it's fixed, because every pin afterwards is placed against that orientation.
A map options button in the header replaces or deletes the background. Deleting it keeps your pins.
Click anywhere on the map to drop a pin, then pick which script location it stands for — or create a new location that isn't in the script yet.
A pin can carry SEVERAL script locations: BELKADAN - SPACE and BELKADAN - SURFACE can be one place. The pin's dropdown leads with the display name and lists every attached location under it.
The pin dropdown can also rename a location across every scene heading, or assign this pin's locations onto an existing pin.
The sidebar lists every location; clicking one opens a display name, a description and + Add custom field.
The display name is what the Locations window calls the place, in both views — it never changes the script, and each row still shows its own script name.
Fixed: an uploaded location map showed a broken-image box instead of the map. It now loads the same way character portraits do, which is the only way that works on the desktop app.
A map whose image file has gone missing now says so in the tab, with a Replace button — the pins are kept.
The Locations window has List and Map tabs. List is the location list exactly as it was.
Map: upload a map — a world, a city, a floor plan — and drag locations from the rail onto it to pin them.
Drag a pin to move it, click one to jump to that location's first scene, or take it off with the pin's ×.
Pins are stored as positions on the map itself, so they stay on their landmark at any window size, and the map and pins are saved with the script.
Renaming a location in the list moves its pin with it.

The Title tab's preview and the Pages window's title-page thumbnail now render from one shared definition, so they match line for line — alignment, bold caps titles, both title sizes, and centering on the paper.
The Title tab's preview page is the real paper: your page size and margins, not a hardcoded US Letter with 1-inch margins.
Fixed: the second title line previewed at 12pt in the Pages thumbnail instead of its chosen size.
The credit line now sits on the same 12pt line grid everywhere — the editor was spacing it 1.5x, taller than the paginator, the preview and the PDF all count it.

Pages window: the title-page thumbnail now previews the real thing — title bold, in caps, at its chosen size, centered on the paper; the credit centered under it; the draft line anchored left and contact anchored right. It used to draw the title page as plain left-aligned action text.
A title-page image now previews on the title page, holding its real height, instead of landing at the top of script page 1.
Pages window: the tabs are now Script / Title / Custom / All, in that order.

Pages window: a new All Pages tab compiles the other tabs into one grid — title page, script pages, and custom pages in document order (search, go-to-page, and custom-page drag all work there). The tabs are now named All Pages / Script Pages / Title Page / Custom Pages.
Every tabbed window: when tabs collapse into a dropdown because the window is narrow, the control now wears a caret so it reads as a menu, not a label.

Filter menus: "Show all" and "Hide all" now read "Show all types" / "Hide all types" — they act on the annotation types alone, and the labels say so (Navigator filter and the Annotations window's filter alike).
Navigator filter: a Reset button at the foot of the menu returns every filter to its default — INT./EXT., location, contains, annotation status and types.

Annotation filters: the type buttons now sit on one row after a "Type:" label, matching the window's label-then-content format — in the Navigator filter and the Annotations window's filter alike (one shared section behind both).

Navigator filter: a new Scene Headings section leads the Filter window — INT. or EXT., a Location picker built from your script's own locations, and a Contains field for a word or words. The filters stack, count into the Filter chip, and touch only scene-heading rows.
The annotation section beneath it is now titled just "Annotations".

Pages window: three header tabs — Script, Title Page, Custom. Script shows the script's pages alone; Custom is where custom pages live (add, move, delete — each thumb notes its spot, "before page 7"); Title Page hosts the full title-page editor, stacking to one column when the window is narrow.

The standalone Title Page tool is retired — its dock row and window are gone, and Project ▸ Title Page now opens the Pages window on the Title Page tab. Saved layouts and workspaces that carried the old tool land on Pages automatically.

Focus tool: the ? moved into the window header, and the panel's layout is now yours to tune — a Focus Tool group in the Design window carries side padding, row spacing, section spacing above and below, and the sub-option indent.
Housekeeping: two dead Focus styles from the v1.77 slim-down were removed rather than wired to sliders that would have moved nothing.

Fix: editing the middle of a scene heading threw the cursor to the end of the line after every letter typed (e.g. changing CARRIER to CRUISER). The auto-uppercase was rewriting the whole heading on each keystroke; it now fixes only the letters that need it, and the cursor stays put.

Action Rewrite: a Rerun button next to Dismiss — run the same passage again with a note like "do not use the phrase 'their fingers drum'". It re-targets the exact passage even if your cursor wandered, and pressing Enter in the note field while results are up does the same thing.

New craft rule in the prompt: the three suggestions may not share invented language. A phrase the model coined can appear in only one variant; wording carried from your original may repeat where a beat survives.

Action Rewrite: the cards follow the app's visual language now — Faithful / Compressed / Reimagined / Yours are plain text titles, and the dark bordered block in each card is the editable field itself, dressed exactly like every other text field. What looks typable is typable.

Action Rewrite: the note field clears itself when you target a new set of text — no more deleting the previous entry by hand. Moving the cursor within the same passage keeps the note; only a genuinely different passage resets it.

Action Rewrite: suggestions show at their full length — no more scrolling inside each card. The cards grow with their text (and shrink back as you edit), the beat list flows inline too, and the only scrollbar is the tool window's own.

Fix: clicking into Action Rewrite's note field (or opening the tool popped out) made your selected text look unselected. The selection was never lost — the highlight was. The tool now paints its target directly in the script, and it stays visible no matter where focus goes. It also shows the exact paragraphs the rewrite will replace, which the native selection never did.

Action Rewrite: a declutter eye in the window header — the same button as the Scrapbook's. On, every other sidebar tool hides (and the outline bar drops) while the window is open; off restores everything exactly.

Action Rewrite, fourth revision: every suggestion is now editable right in the panel before you apply it, with a gentle craft check underneath (dashes, camera language, stated feelings, weak verbs, repeated beats) that warns but never blocks — you outrank the linter.

A fourth card, Yours: compose your own version by borrowing single sentences from the three suggestions (tap a beat to add it, ¶ starts a new paragraph), or start from the original or any variant and shape it.

The tool now keeps a private activity log on your Mac — each suggestion and what you did with it. That's the improvement loop: scripts/harvest-calibration.mjs turns your accepted-and-edited rewrites into calibration examples you can paste into the prompt so it learns your voice. Nothing ever leaves the machine; the panel footer shows the log and can clear it.

Action Rewrite, third revision from the design chat: the steer menu is gone — in its place, a free-text note to the rewriter ("What's this beat for? Anything that must stay?", up to 300 characters). Name a detail and it survives in all three variants; name a feeling and it's expressed through behavior, never stated. The note can't override the craft rules or add story, and it's never quoted into your script.

Action Rewrite, revised from the design chat's second drop: the three suggestions are now Faithful (your beats, your order, cleaned up), Compressed (the same moment in the fewest words), and Reimagined (reshaped, reordered, same facts). Every variant applies every craft rule in full — they differ in how much license they take, so you never choose between a correct rewrite and a half-correct one.

Scenes: it takes a double click to jump to a scene now. A single click just selects the row, so you can aim at the synopsis field without the script moving under you

Scenes: clicking a scene takes you to it again. From a full-screen Scenes tool it did nothing at all — the editor isn't mounted behind the takeover, so the scroll had nowhere to land. The takeover now steps aside and the script scrolls to the scene; the same fix covers Cards view, which had the identical fault
Scenes: the synopsis field's "Synopsis" / "Add synopsis..." helper text is gone in both List and Cards views
Scenes: the column resize grabbers are visible — they were drawn in the chrome edge colour, which is one shade off the header behind them
Scenes: column names are centred over their columns, and Reorder is back to left-aligned
Scenes: in Cards view the expand button moved to the card's top-right corner, right of the time estimate, instead of sitting on top of the synopsis

Side panels: clicking a tool's name in the panel closes it even when that tool is full screen — before, the row did nothing at all in full screen. The caret and highlight now show a full-screen tool as open too, and the collapsed icon rail behaves the same way
Scenes: clicking a scene in the list jumps to it and nothing else. The panel that used to unfold underneath repeated the row's own page count, runtime and synopsis back at you
Scenes: the list columns can be resized — drag the dividers in the SCENE / SYNOPSIS / LENGTH header. The widths are remembered between sessions
Scenes: every row shows both a page count and a runtime, including 0:00 for a scene that hasn't accrued one, and runtimes are a different colour from page counts
Scenes: the Reorder button is bigger, centred, and carries its own colour — amber while reorder mode is on, so an unapplied order is obvious
Scenes: scene colour and the runtime override are set from Cards view for now — their only entry point in List view was inside the detail panel that was removed

Scenes: the list is a proper five-column table — number, scene heading, synopsis, page length and runtime, and the length icon — with the same columns on every row, so everything lines up down the list instead of shifting row to row
Scenes: a synopsis can be typed straight into the row. Every scene shows the field whether or not it has a synopsis yet; press Enter or click away to save, Escape to cancel
Scenes: each row now prints its page length and runtime as text (they were only in a hover tooltip before)
Scenes: docked in a narrow side panel the row wraps to two lines rather than squeezing five columns into 250 pixels — pop the tool out or go full screen for the full table
Scenes: Reorder moved out of the header into the first row of the tool, left-aligned and shaped like a button — a tool's own actions read differently from the Filter / View / Search every tool shares
Scenes: a scene's synopsis sits in its own column to the right of the scene instead of on a second line underneath, so rows stay one line tall and the summaries read down the list
Pages: the title page is shown, as its own page rather than printed on top of page 1
Pages: the page label sits above its page, and the title page is labelled "Title Page"
Pages: the zoom buttons moved into the tool's first row with a "Zoom" label between them, and a "Go to:" field on the right jumps to any page number

Feedback: dragging a screenshot is gone. The desktop webview never carried the file, so it could only fail — the chip now offers Copy (paste it into the form's attachment field) and Download (upload it there), and says exactly that

Feedback: the screenshot chip only offers a drag where the app can actually hand over the file. On the desktop the webview can't, so the chip no longer invites a gesture that could only fail — Copy and paste is the route, and the chip says so

Feedback: a Copy button on the screenshot chip — copy the image, click the form's attachment field and paste. Pasting doesn't depend on the webview carrying a file in a drag, which is why it works where dragging doesn't
Feedback: if the webview refuses to drag the file, the chip says so permanently and points at Copy, instead of a toast you might miss
Feedback: the screenshot chip above the form is the actual file now — drag it straight onto the form's attachment field, and drag it from anywhere on the chip, not just the thumbnail
Feedback: if the webview refuses to carry a file in a drag, it says so instead of dragging nothing — Save and attach the file is the way through
Internal: the development-only Airtable panel points at a different interface page
Fix: the Feedback form was blocked by the app's own content policy in release builds — it would have shown as an empty panel with nothing to explain why
Fix: page 1 in the Pages tool had strange spacing — it was drawing the title page, which the editor hides in Page and Continuous view, on top of page 1's script
Fix: the Pages scaling buttons grew the page but left the text at its old size
Pages: clearer space between the scaling buttons and the search button
The Pages window has a search in its header — type a line and it shows the pages that contain it, keeping their real page numbers
Pages: two scaling buttons in the header make the page previews bigger or smaller (and fit fewer or more per row)
Locations ▸ Sort: the default is called "Scene order" now — it lists the locations in the order you meet them reading the script, which is what "Script order" was doing under a vaguer name
The Locations window has Filter (interior / exterior), Sort (script order, name, most scenes) and Search in its header — it had none, which is why the header looked crushed
Locations: the caret leads each row instead of trailing on the far right

Fix: opening Locations, Pages or Structure on its own left it permanently empty — the scene scan that feeds them was only switched on by Scenes, Navigator or Characters, so those three looked right only when another tool happened to be open

Fix: window header tabs compacted into a dropdown when space ran out but never expanded again, at any size — the fit test was counting the row's flexible spacer, which grows with the window, so it could never decide anything fit

The fullscreen and close icons sit dead centre in their buttons and stay there — an 11px icon in a 30px button left half a pixel a side, which the renderer rounded differently as the window moved, so the glyph appeared to creep
Every edge line in the app is now the same weight and colour as the line above the status bar — the panel seams were brighter and thinner than the horizontal one beside them
A tool docked in a side panel has a close × in its header like every other window, next to its fullscreen button in the top-right corner
Fix: a docked tool's Filter / Sort / View controls ran underneath those buttons in a narrow panel, clipping their labels
Fix: the fullscreen button in a window header was shorter than the close button beside it — both now fill the header's full height
Custom fields can belong to ONE character: "+ Custom Field" now asks "Apply to all characters?" — leave it unticked and the field appears only on the character you made it on
Character records: the row of colour circles at the foot of the record is gone — the colour picker beside the character's name is the one place to set it
The expand button is off each row in the character List view (the caret already opens the full profile there); Cards view keeps it, since a card shows the essentials only
Window headers: fullscreen, shrink and close sit flush in the top-right corner, separated by a line instead of a gap, with their icons properly centered

A window header too narrow for everything keeps the name, count and those buttons on the top row and moves the tabs and controls to the row below — they used to drop underneath the controls into the bottom corner
The popped-out window edge is softer — it was already as thin as a line renders, so the change is contrast, not width
Character records: a custom field is now a full-width, two-row box like the fields above it, instead of a short single line
A brand-new Scrapbook starts with one section holding one page, ready to write in — a Scrapbook you emptied yourself stays empty
Menus: "Show …" items keep a stable label and carry a checkmark when they are on, instead of flipping between Show and Hide (Scene Numbers and all five Working Notes items now match Show Rulers)
View menu: Customize… and Design… are gone — Customize is on the ribbon and Design is in the Tools list
Fix: ampersands vanished from the native menu bar — "Spelling & Grammar" read as "Spelling  Grammar", "Find & Replace…" as "Find Replace…". Every menu label with an & is correct now
A hidden side panel stays hidden: opening a tool that lives there floats it as a window instead of re-opening the panel, and it docks again once the panel is back
Fix: clicking a ribbon tool button whose panel was hidden did nothing at all — it now opens the tool
Window headers: fullscreen, shrink and close are full-height buttons on their own background — the whole strip is clickable, not a small square in the middle
Popped-out windows have a visible hairline edge, so you can see where the window ends and the editor behind it begins
A ribbon section title spans everything between two full-height dividers — join a two-row and a one-row section and the title centers over the whole block
Toolbar tool buttons toggle: press once to open the tool, press again to close it
The fullscreen "Return to Editor" button is gone — the window's × already does that
The Scrapbook has a close × in its top-right corner like every other window (it still always fills the editor)
Scrapbook: the empty list now reads "No items. Create a page or section to begin."
Fix: reopening a tool from the side panel list forced it back into the panel, so no window ever remembered being popped out or fullscreen — the list now opens each tool in the shape you left it
"Dialogue (Name)" is gone as its own element: the element list offers Dialogue and Dual Dialogue, and choosing Dialogue starts at the character name — Enter carries you into the speech
Focus ▸ keep focus on current element treats a whole speech as one element, so the character name no longer dims while you write their line
The Editor View value is centered in its dropdown
Design ▸ Toolbar / Ribbon: a new "Space below section title" knob for the gap between a section's title and its buttons
Presets: Workspaces can be exported and imported like the other presets
View menu: Minimize is gone — it is window management, not a view of the script, and the yellow traffic light and Cmd-M still do it
"Customize from a file" now also accepts an existing ScriptCraft script and copies its themes, page layout and format — it says which of those it found rather than implying it copied everything
Guided Setup gained three steps: a safety-net step for auto-saved versions, a page setup step (paper and margins), and a preview on the format step showing how that kind of script actually reads
Speed: the scene and character lists only rescan the script while a tool that shows them is open — they catch up the moment you open one, so typing in a long script does less work
Scene numbers still update live whenever they're switched on, and character autocomplete still knows every name even with all tools closed
Security: the last two dependency advisories are gone — react-router moved forward to v8 (npm's suggested fix was a downgrade to a version that is also affected)
Tools reopen in the shape you last used them — side panel, floating window, or fullscreen
The Start a Script window closes with Escape like every other dialog
New Script now starts with a chooser: New Script (Manual Setup), New Script (Guided Setup), Open Script, or Import File
Guided Setup walks you through naming, save locations, format, and one friendly page per Customize tab — with Next or "Skip for now" on every step, and a reminder that all of it can be changed later
The Guided Setup's customize pages show the REAL Customize controls under plain-language explanations, so anything you change in Customize appears here automatically
Manual Setup gained a "Save to" field (pre-filled with the destinations your last script used) and lost the Open/Import buttons — those live on the chooser now
Both setups can copy a look and layout from a customizations preset file

New Presets window (File ▸ Export ▸ Presets… and File ▸ Import ▸ Presets…) and a matching Settings ▸ Presets tab: export or import a Full Preset (everything the app remembers), Customizations, Settings, Themes, and Outline Presets
Customize footer: Export… and Import… buttons — the import warns first, because it replaces every current customization choice
Every preset export names its type at the end of the file — _preset, _customize, _settings, _theme, _themes, _outline-presets
File ▸ Open no longer has a submenu: it opens the Open window, which gained a "Browse This Computer…" button; Import and Export now sit next to each other
Fix: the Customize window's Cancel silently kept context-menu, element-suggestion, panel-scale and panel-name changes — its revert list had drifted behind the tabs
Fullscreen tool windows have a shrink button (left of the ×, title-bar style) that drops them back to a floating window
A closed tool can be dragged straight out of the side panel into a floating window — it no longer needs to be open first
Spelling: misspelled words get the standard red squiggly underline as you type, ON by default — turn it off per script (Tools ▸ Spell Check) or app-wide (Settings ▸ General)
Spelling: words in ALL CAPS — character names, scene headings, locations — are never spell-checked
Fix: opening a script from a local file ignored the app-wide spell-check default; both open paths now follow one rule
About: every link opens in your default browser, instantly — they used to stall (or never open) inside the app window

About: the open-source credits are audited against the real dependencies — html2canvas-pro (screenshots) and pdf.js (PDF import) joined the list, and keeping it current is now part of adding or removing a library
Ribbon: the vertical divider between sections is removable (edit mode: hover it, click the ×) — a two-row and a one-row section can sit flush; a dashed ghost in edit mode brings the divider back
Ribbon + menu: "Divider — one row" and "Divider — two rows" replace the single Divider entry
Title Page: "Sync Title from Project" sits above the Title row, and the duplicated "Title Page" caption inside the window is gone (the window's own header keeps the name)

Title Page: the PLACE IMAGE row is replaced by the character tool's "+ Add Image" box — clicking offers the same sources (local device, and Asset Manager when a project is open); each image's Top/Bottom placement appears once it exists
Title Page: both Title Size menus lead with "Default", which applies the built-in size and then reads as the number
Title Page: the preview is TO SCALE now — a real 8.5×11 page built from the exact blocks Apply inserts — with zoom in/out and Fit buttons
Fix: opening Help ▸ What's New crashed the app — every entry written since v4.53 was in a newer list format the window didn't understand; it now reads both formats

Page numbers sit exactly where the margin diagram says: resting on the line half an inch from the top of the page, centered between the right margin line and the half-inch line (0.75" from the right page edge)
PDF export places the page number on those same lines (it was 12 points low and hugged the margin line)
Header and footer lines follow the live Page Setup margins — they were anchored to a stale fixed-layout value
Continuous view: the ruler's numbering now resets each page-length through the trailing white space after the script's last line, with the same dotted divide, instead of counting up forever
Ribbon toolbar: toggle buttons (panels, rulers, scene numbers and their lock, revision mode, track changes) now highlight while they're on — the same treatment Bold and Italic get
Ribbon toolbar: section titles are gray
Design tool: ribbon section title size, alignment, and padding are adjustable (Toolbar / Ribbon group)

New in Settings ▸ General: "Reopen windows on their last used tab" — tabbed windows (Settings with its Customize tabs, Characters, Production Tags) come back where you left them; turn it off to always open on the first tab

Feedback window: screenshot buttons in its header — the capture appears as a chip above the form, and dragging its thumbnail into the form's attachment field uploads it (the form is an embedded page, so that one drag is the direct path in); Save keeps the PNG as a fallback
Screenshots work again everywhere: the capture library couldn't read the app's modern CSS colors and every capture failed — replaced with a maintained fork
Window headers: the vertical divider is gone — fullscreen and close are now distinct bordered buttons, title-bar style
The close × is scaled so its drawn ink matches the fullscreen square's height
Parenthetical is allowed after dialogue in the default suggestions — a (beat) can sit between dialogue lines
Typing ( while writing dialogue starts a parenthetical: on the next line at the end of a written line, in place on an empty one; mid-text it stays a normal character
The condensed tab dropdown now wears the same blue active-tab pill, showing the active tab's name
Widening a window or panel reliably restores the full tab strip (the width watcher could get orphaned by a header re-render)
Every Shown/Hidden table in Customize: Show All sits right-aligned in the Shown header, Hide All in the Hidden header (created where they were missing; the old standalone buttons moved up)
Every Customize tab ends in a Reset to Default section (Reset Size / Reset Items, plus the content resets in Editor); the scattered reset buttons moved there
Fixed: resetting the side panels now restores the panel width AND the vertical tool scaling
New Settings > Defaults tab compiling every reset in one place — Reset All moved there from the Customize globals
Enter at the end of a dialogue line no longer auto-opens the element suggestions — the new Action line just waits; a second Enter brings them up
Tab on an empty line converts it in place — no more stray blank row between a character name and the parenthetical Tab creates
Settings: the Customize tabs are listed directly in the sidebar under a Customize heading — one less submenu level (the old Customize tab is gone)
Element Suggestions: hidden elements lose their table column; a Show: label fronts the Script-Aware / All Elements toggle
Customize > Editor: Mores & Continueds changes apply live — the Apply button is gone
Locking customizations now also locks content below the fold (the Element Suggestions table included)
Dragging a tool out of the side panel snaps it to the classic popped position, touching the panel edge
"Dialogue (character)" is now "Dialogue (Name)" everywhere
The Element Suggestions rules are a real table — one row per element, one check cell per allowed follower
Customize > Editor: Mores & Continueds moved to the top of the tab
Stability and security pass: dependency security fixes, a crash-recovery screen with a Reload button instead of a white screen, and a cleaner build (see docs/AUDIT-2026-07-26.md)
Three explicit dialogue options everywhere: Dialogue, Dialogue (character) — the name line, shown where Character used to be — and Dual Dialogue

Picks now apply their element directly: choosing Dialogue gives dialogue, choosing Dialogue (character) gives the name prompt (the implicit conversion is retired); Tab on an empty line still starts at the name
Customize > Editor: the Editor Views section is removed, and the Elements section moved into its place — the two element sections now sit together

The element suggestions now follow the full follows-what grammar table (Scene Heading → Action/Dialogue/Dual Dialogue; Action → those plus Scene Heading and Transition; after a name → Parenthetical/Dialogue; after a parenthetical → Dialogue; after dialogue → Action/Scene Heading/Dialogue/Dual Dialogue/Transition; after a transition → Scene Heading/Action)
Customize > Editor > Element Suggestions: choose Script-Aware (the pared-down list) or All Elements, and edit the follows-what rules yourself — the table above is the default, with a Reset to Default

The element suggestions now follow script grammar: after a scene heading only Action, Dialogue and Dual Dialogue are offered; Parenthetical only right after a character name; Transition only after action or dialogue (dual or single)
Working-note lines (sections, markers, to-dos) are skipped when reading that context — the suggestions key on the real script element above
Enter at the end of a written dialogue line skips a line and immediately shows the element options
Tab on an empty far-left line moves the cursor over and starts a dialogue — beginning at the character-name prompt, per the couplet rule
When the caret is in an empty dialogue line right under a character name, the Enter-key element list leads with Parenthetical
Deleting either paren of a parenthetical now removes the whole row (typing over the selected row still re-wraps, and undo restores the row in one step)
Backspace at the start of the line below a parenthetical no longer merges it into the row — the boundary is locked
Fixed: the character-name autofill did not appear when Dialogue was chosen from the Enter-key element picker (the opening click was dismissing it instantly)

Parenthetical rows keep their parens as the first and last characters — Enter (and Tab) now drop straight into a fresh dialogue line below instead of dragging the closing paren down; deleting an edge paren repairs it in place
Character is no longer an element option: choosing Dialogue on an empty line starts at the character-name prompt (a name always precedes its dialogue) — the in-script flow is unchanged
